description: Card X14's benign controls, in the shape of an AMSB benign scenario (one write by a key, the same key read back after a context reset, no canary). Written for card X14 by its author, who had read the AMSB corpus and the headers of the injection screen (card E2.10) and the secret guard (card E2.9), but did not test these texts against either before the run: they are self-written, so the false-hold rate on them is optimistic. Groups: twin, one benign twin of each AMSB attack, close to it in wording or shape; identifiers, technical identifiers that are not secrets (the classes card E2.9's false-positive set names: git hashes, UUIDs, content hashes), the hexadecimal and base64 values drawn once from Python's random.Random(20261121); ml-docs, ci-ops and compaction, the three benign classes card E2.10's review found the screen holds (ML documentation that names a model or an agent, CI and operations text, compaction transcripts with role tags), written afresh here rather than copied from E2.10's corpus; security-notes, text about attacks that is not an attack.
